title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: In the post-pandemic era, Employers’ and Business Membership Organizations (EBMOs) across the Asia-Pacific region face challenges in strengthening financial sustainability, enhancing their value proposition to members, and helping companies reshape work and business models to strengthen competitiveness in digital transformation. The ILO has provided technical assistance by customizing tested global approaches to achieve economies of scale, enabling cost-effective replicable solutions and knowledge-sharing. Efforts have been made to expand the use of digital channels to assist EBMOs with member engagement, data collection, analysis, research, and thought leadership. Enhanced coordination and partnerships with other business organizations have been promoted to increase the effectiveness and relevance of EBMOs and to advocate for productivity growth and an enabling environment for sustainable enterprises. For the current biennium, the ILO's efforts aim to enhance the capacity of EBMOs to serve their members in a new and unpredictable environment, invest in resilience, and promote a more integrated and unified private sector voice. By focusing on strategic planning, policy engagement, and capacity building, the ILO seeks to support EBMOs in strengthening their financial sustainability and value proposition, ensuring they can effectively represent the interests of both domestic enterprises and foreign investors. The strategy focuses on organizing sub-regional forums and inter-regional exchanges to enhance the strategy for greater organizational value and resilience. This includes sub-regional conferences in ASEAN and the Pacific to share research findings and experiences on the future of work, financial sustainability, and strategic planning. The strategy also involves regional workshops and support services on Responsible Business Conduct (RBC/ESG) for EBMOs, including the development of technical information products and policy development tools.
